newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rescuers confirm death of French climbers.
newsitem.headline: Peru rescuers confirm death of French climbers.

text.p: Peruvian rescuers said on Wednesday they had found the corpses of two French climbers who fell into a ravine while scaling an Andean peak.

Police rescue officer Max Portocarrero said the pair, whom he identified as Jean Lebaux, 25, and Ivan Murador, 28, were found under 33 feet (10 metres) of snow near the summit of the 19,540-foot (5,960 metre) Mount Alpamayo in northern Peru.
Their bodies were due to be taken to the nearby town of Huaraz.
"We presume there was a dislodging of snow which fell down and knocked them off as they were scaling an ice-face," Portocarrero told Reuters.

The Frenchmen went missing on June 28, just days after another French climber, Etienne Girard, 28, and Peruvian guide Cesar Henostroza Gloria, 27, also died after being caught by an avalanche in the same Cordillera Blanca or White Range of mountains.
